Definition: from G80; brotherhood (properly, the feeling of brotherliness), i.e. the (Christian) fraternity:--brethren, brotherhood.
BiblicalUsage: Adelphotes is the brotherhood itself — the whole company of believers, named as one body. Peter uses it twice: once in the command to honour everyone and love the brotherhood, and once in the assurance that the same sufferings are being endured by the brotherhood throughout the world. It is the only place the word appears, and both times it gathers scattered Christians into a single family.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word is a comfort to anyone who feels alone in their faith. The brotherhood is worldwide, and the suffering you face is shared — you are not the only one standing, and you are not standing alone.
